provenance.what: The language-neutral oracle for engine-surface RETENTION: which window's pointer-dispatchable engine surfaces survive a frame, given what that frame repainted and which window instances the layout still names.
provenance.why: The wgpu shell mirrored its bespoke pointer-state maps (`node_graph_states`/`tiled_map_states`/`board2d_states`) from the per-frame PAINT drain and evicted every surface absent from it. Retained painting means a window whose document did not change does not repaint, so the node-graph surface fell out of the map in nearly every frame — and while it is absent no pointer, wheel, context menu, catalogue drop or `Fit graph` chrome control can reach it (`node_graph_pointer_down_into` is only ever called for a surface that is in the map). `world3d_states` was never evicted that way and its input worked, which is the asymmetry this oracle closes. Ticket 26/09/09/PROCEDURAL-3D-END-TO-END, 📓️wgpu-retained-controls-wires-2026-09-13.md §7.3(b).
provenance.rule: An engine surface's pointer state is owned by its WINDOW INSTANCE, not by a painted frame. Absence from a frame's paint drain means 'this window did not repaint', never 'this surface died'.
provenance.reference: React already holds this rule structurally: `🕸️NodeGraph/🟦️.tsx`'s host effect is keyed on `[surfaceId]` alone and its cleanup is documented as 'A retained surface host unmounts exactly once, when its window closes' — never on a render or a paint.

rules.ownerIsTheWindowInstance: Every retained engine surface names the window instance whose body it is painted into. That window's presence in the frame's layout — the dock window plan plus the open panels — is the ONLY thing that keeps the surface alive.
rules.aFrameWithoutARepaintKeepsTheSurface: A frame whose paint drain does not mention a surface leaves that surface exactly as it was: same bounds, same controller, still resolvable by a pointer inside its bounds.
rules.aRepaintRefreshesTheProjection: A drain that does mention the surface overwrites its bounds and controller with what was just painted, so a moved or resized pane dispatches against its new rectangle.
rules.aClosedWindowDropsItsSurface: The frame in which a surface's owning window leaves the layout is the frame its pointer state is dropped. Nothing under the old rectangle is dispatchable afterwards.
rules.creationIsAnnouncedOnce: A drain reports the surfaces whose engine host was constructed on it, and only those — the app-static catalogue is installed on exactly those and never re-pushed per frame.
rules.everyCompositedKindIsRetainedAlike: NodeGraph, TiledMap and Board2d follow one rule, and it is the rule World3d already followed: one owner of engine-surface state per window instance, independent of repaint.

windows.why: One mode's dock: the Flow canvas that carries the node graph, a preview pane, and a panel-hosted board. `procedural-main` is the window id the wgpu dock plan really names for the Flow canvas on 6118.

cases.name: a-painted-surface-becomes-pointer-dispatchable
cases.why: The baseline: the frame that paints the graph is the frame its pointer state appears.

cases.name: a-frame-without-a-repaint-keeps-the-surface
cases.why: THE defect. A retained document that did not change does not repaint, so its surface is absent from the drain — and the graph stopped being reachable by any pointer at all.

cases.name: a-repaint-refreshes-the-projection
cases.why: Retention must not freeze a stale rectangle: the drain that does paint the surface is authoritative for where it is and who answers for it.

cases.name: a-closed-window-drops-its-surface
cases.why: The other half of the rule: retention is not immortality. A mode switch that removes the Flow window must take its hit rectangle with it, or a click on whatever replaces it dispatches into a graph nobody can see.

cases.name: every-composited-kind-is-retained-alike
cases.why: The tiled map and the 2-D board were evicted by the very same drain rule and inherit the very same fix — one rule, three kinds, no per-kind exception.

cases.name: creation-is-announced-once
cases.why: The catalogue install rides on this list. Announcing a surface twice re-pushes ~100 kB per frame; announcing it never leaves the graph without its operator palette.
